elements_not_encoded.text: Give emergency contraception if patient had unprotected sex in past 5 days and does not want pregnancy:
elements_not_encoded.reason: Box header is the indication for giving emergency contraception (a management action). No diagnosis or priority is stated, so no check_for/priority rule; 'does not want pregnancy' also has no SNOMED finding (see remaining questions).

elements_not_encoded.text: Check pregnancy test and if negative, insert Copper IUD1 as soon as possible or give single dose levonorgestrel 1.5mg orally.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Pregnancy test then Copper IUD or levonorgestrel 1.5mg: test and treatment steps; no manage tasks in this pass.

elements_not_encoded.text: If patient > 80kg, BMI2 ≥ 30, or on efavirenz, rifampicin, phenytoin or carbamazepine, offer Copper IUD1 or increase dose of levonorgestrel to 3mg.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Dose/method choice by weight, BMI and interacting drugs; medicine selection, not triage.

elements_not_encoded.text: If patient on ketoconazole/fluconazole, advise levonorgestrel may cause nausea/vomiting and offer Copper IUD1 instead.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Advice and method choice for patients on ketoconazole/fluconazole.

elements_not_encoded.text: If patient vomits < 2 hours after taking levonorgestrel, repeat dose.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Repeat dose if vomiting < 2 hours after levonorgestrel; medicine instruction.

elements_not_encoded.text: Offer to start long-term contraceptive at same visit (if IUD not chosen). If injectable or implant given, check pregnancy test in 2 weeks.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Start long-term contraception; follow-up pregnancy test in 2 weeks.

elements_not_encoded.text: Assess for HIV and hepatitis B post-exposure prophylaxis 119. Advise patient to return for pregnancy test if next period is more than 7 days late.
elements_not_encoded.reason: PEP assessment is a cross-reference to 119 plus return advice for a late period; management/follow-up.

judgment_calls.topic: Red box not encoded as rules
judgment_calls.decision: Every red-box element is a management step (emergency contraception, doses, PEP, follow-up). The box does not say 'urgent attention', so no priority evaluation was invented and no check_for task was made from it.
judgment_calls.alternatives: An Urgent priority or a check_for task on (<= (onset Unprotected sexual intercourse) (time_ago 5 days)); rejected because the page states no priority and nothing on the page would consume the checked findings.

judgment_calls.topic: Scope of 'when using combined oral contraceptive'
judgment_calls.decision: Applied to nausea, breast tenderness and missed period alike: possible pregnancy needs COC use AND any one symptom.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Qualifier applies only to 'missed period' (nausea or breast tenderness alone in any contraception user would then suggest pregnancy; rule would fire more often).

judgment_calls.decision: STI symptoms -> 62, BP >= 140/90 -> 148, BMI >= 25 -> 156, breast lumps -> 55/42, menopause -> 187, HIV -> 124/126/119 are cross-references or management and are not encoded on this page.
judgment_calls.alternatives: check_for tasks for these findings; rejected because no rule on this page consumes them (would break Will's constraint 2) and the page draws no 'likely/consider' conclusion from them.
